name: Cloud Application
difference: The draft emphasizes greenfield PaaS design; the book broadens the architecture discussion.
intro: Design an application around cloud capabilities so it can evolve and use resources effectively.

name: Big Ball of Mud
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Get early functionality working quickly when the requirements and value of an application are still uncertain.

name: Modular Monolith
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Keep one deployable application while organizing its code into maintainable, cohesive modules.

name: Distributed Architecture
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Allow parts of an application to be developed, deployed, and executed independently.

name: Cloud-Native Architecture
difference: A short source-repository draft, absent from the homepage navigation.
intro: Structure an application to benefit from the platform on which it runs.

name: Application Package
difference: Related predecessor, not an exact rename: the book covers packaging, dependencies and deployment; use the book for those aspects.
intro: Choose a language and toolchain that bundle the application with its required dependencies for deployment.

name: Service API
difference: The draft emphasizes HTTP and REST; the book includes a broader service contract discussion.
intro: Expose application tasks through a contract that clients can invoke without knowing the implementation.

name: Stateless Application
difference: The draft stores session state in a backend service; the book emphasizes client-held session context passed in requests. Both keep durable domain state outside application processes.
intro: Handle concurrent requests and recover from process failures without keeping essential data inside the application instance.

name: Replicable Application
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Run equivalent application instances to maintain service through failures and increasing demand.

name: External Configuration
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Deploy one application build into different environments by supplying settings separately from code.

name: Backend Service
difference: Short draft; book supplies the fuller discussion.
intro: Share reusable functionality across applications through a separately running service.

name: Microservices
difference: The book list says Microservices; the chapter heading and contents say Microservice.
intro: Organize an application into cooperating modules that teams can develop independently.

name: Domain Microservice
difference: Website filename differs from its Domain Microservice title.
intro: Assign each business capability to a service that encapsulates its logic and exposes a cohesive API.

name: Adapter Microservice
difference: Same core identity.
intro: Reuse existing functionality through a service boundary that fits a microservices application.

name: Dispatcher
difference: The draft explicitly calls a BFF a Dispatcher.
intro: Give each client channel a suitable interface over business functionality spread across several services.

name: Polyglot Development
difference: Same core identity.
intro: Let service teams choose implementation languages suited to their responsibilities.

name: Self-Managed Data Store
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback. The chapter heading is plural; retain the singular list identity.
intro: Give each stateful microservice exclusive control over its persistent data.

name: Service Orchestrator
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Coordinate several service operations behind one API task that performs a larger business activity.

name: Model Around the Domain
difference: Related draft: maps the design process broadly; book provides the named pattern.
intro: Bring stakeholders together to describe the domain and reveal the capabilities the application must provide.

name: Ubiquitous Language
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Use shared domain vocabulary to reduce misunderstandings between stakeholders and developers.

unavailable.sketch: The supporting discussion supplies verbal domain examples rather than a standalone language diagram.

name: Event Storming
difference: Despite the filename, the draft describes the Event Storming workshop, not the book pattern Domain Event.
intro: Explore domain events with stakeholders to uncover behavior, concepts, and candidate boundaries.

name: Domain Event
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Represent a meaningful occurrence in the domain so other parts of the system can respond.

name: Bounded Context
difference: Draft defines team boundaries; the book also covers domain semantics and context mapping.
intro: Define a boundary within which domain terminology, rules, and concepts have a consistent meaning.

name: Application Services
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Protect a bounded context’s internals behind operations that serve application use cases.

unavailable.forces: The embedded supporting passage does not develop a separate forces discussion.
unavailable.sketch: No standalone application-service figure is supplied in the cited passage.
unavailable.consequences: No separate benefit/liability discussion is given for this supporting pattern.
unavailable.examples: No standalone application-service example is developed in the cited passage.

name: Context Map
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Make the relationships and boundaries between domain contexts visible to technical and business stakeholders.

unavailable.forces: The supporting passage describes a mapping method without a standalone forces section.
unavailable.consequences: No distinct trade-off discussion for Context Map is given; adjacent consequences belong to Bounded Context.

name: Aggregate
difference: The draft combines entities and aggregates; this catalog follows the book aggregate identity.
intro: Group tightly related domain entities and values so they can be treated as one cohesive concept.

name: Repositories
difference: Listed twice on book p. iv; the main-list description incorrectly repeats Refactor then Extract. Use the supporting-list description and p. 215.
intro: Mediate between aggregates and persistent storage through a domain-oriented collection interface.

unavailable.examples: The supporting passage does not develop a separate repository example; the following customer/order example illustrates Aggregate.

name: Domain Service
difference: Draft uses Services as its title.
intro: Model business operations that belong to the domain but not to one entity or aggregate.

name: Anti-Corruption Layer
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Let bounded contexts communicate while protecting their distinct domain models.

name: Event Choreography
difference: The draft presents the architecture broadly; the book names its coordination pattern Event Choreography.
intro: Let independently interested components react when another component changes.

name: Event
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Represent a component’s change as information that other components can interpret.

name: Reactive Component
difference: Related narrower draft: consumption is one role; the book covers components that consume and emit.
intro: Build a component that listens for relevant events and chooses an appropriate response.

name: Event Notifier
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Announce significant component changes as events for interested participants.

name: Event API
difference: Related narrower draft: a registry publishes contracts, while the book defines the contract itself.
intro: Define which events components can expect and how those events are represented.

name: Event Backbone
difference: Same core identity.
intro: Deliver events to interested components without directly coupling them to their producers.

name: Event Sourcing
difference: The draft uses ride-hailing; the book expands replay, checkpoints, retention and external-system limitations.
intro: Retain an ordered event history to explain and reconstruct how application state developed.

name: Cloud Database
difference: Related draft shares externalized persistent state; book expands cloud database topology.
intro: Persist application data in storage designed to operate reliably and scale in a cloud environment.

name: Replicated Database
difference: No single standalone draft covers the book pattern. Synchronous Replication and Asynchronous Replication are related draft strategies, not additional book-list identities; use the book for the integrated treatment.
intro: Maintain redundant database nodes and copies so storage can match an application’s availability and capacity needs.

name: Configuration Database
difference: Global Configs is a three-line predecessor about cross-datacenter configuration; the book develops reliable service-state coordination, consistency and change notifications. The book supplies the missing aspects.
intro: Keep shared service state consistent and accessible across the nodes of a distributed cloud service.

name: Application Database
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Store domain data in a database whose availability, capacity, and access model support a stateless application.

name: Relational Database
difference: The draft explicitly recommends a relational DBMS.
intro: Persist structured data that needs flexible queries and relationships between records.

name: Document Database
difference: Draft emphasizes JSON responses; book addresses evolving document structure more generally.
intro: Store evolving domain entities as documents when their future structure is not fully known.

name: Key-Value Database
difference: Same storage model with a revised name.
intro: Store independent values for fast retrieval through a known key.

name: Graph Database
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Store connected entities so applications can follow their relationships efficiently.

name: Columnar Database
difference: The draft emphasizes fixed or slowly changing schemas and slower writes; the book discusses semi-structured data and groups wide-column stores with column-oriented analytics. Retain this source ambiguity rather than assuming all examples have one layout or workload profile.
intro: Organize analytical data for queries that inspect selected attributes across many records.

name: Data Module
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Align cohesive groups of stored data with application modules so both can evolve more independently.

name: Polyglot Persistence
difference: Same core identity.
intro: Store each data module using the database model that fits its structure and access patterns.

name: Database-as-a-Service
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Obtain an application database through a service that handles much of its provisioning and management.

name: Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS)
difference: The website uses Separation rather than Segregation and emphasizes coexistence with a legacy write model. The book emphasizes concurrent queries and updates and presents a two-database design.
intro: Separate query and update responsibilities so each can serve its own access and throughput needs.

name: Client Application
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Provide a user-facing application that accesses services running in the cloud.

name: Browser Application
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Reach users through a web browser without requiring a particular installed client platform.

name: Web Form Application
difference: The draft means server-generated forms; the book separates Browser Application from Web Form Application.
intro: Deliver basic functionality widely through server-generated pages and HTML forms.

name: Single-Page Application
difference: Hyphenation differs.
intro: Handle browser interaction within one logical page to balance responsiveness and server communication.

name: Micro Frontend
difference: Same core identity.
intro: Divide a large frontend into independently owned business features instead of one shared application.

name: Mobile Application
difference: The book uses a broader title.
intro: Tailor the user experience to mobile devices and their platform-specific capabilities.

name: Command-Line Interface
difference: Hyphenation differs.
intro: Enable bulk, repeated, or scheduled operations through commands that invoke application services.

name: Public API
difference: Same core identity.
intro: Expose a deliberate interface for third-party applications to use cloud application functionality.

name: Interaction Model
difference: Same core identity.
intro: Separate user-interaction state and flow from presentation code and business logic.

name: Lift and Shift
difference: Same core identity.
intro: Move an existing application to cloud infrastructure with minimal changes to its implementation.

name: Virtualize the Application
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Package an installed application in a virtual server that can run in compatible environments.

name: Containerize the Application
difference: Book title also accommodates applications that are not monoliths.
intro: Package an application for denser deployment and portability across compatible container environments.

name: Refactor the Monolith
difference: Draft focuses on cloud dependencies; book addresses maintainability and distribution together.
intro: Improve an existing application’s structure so teams can maintain it and prepare parts for distributed execution.

name: Start Small
difference: Same core identity.
intro: Begin cloud adoption with a limited working change that lets the organization learn before expanding.

name: Pave the Road
difference: Same core identity.
intro: Make cloud adoption easier through shared infrastructure, examples, training, and development practices.

name: Strangle the Monolith
difference: Also appears in Cloud-Adoption/Strangler-App; one book identity with two drafts.
intro: Replace monolithic functionality incrementally with microservices while the existing system continues to provide value.

name: Wrap the Monolith
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback. The book calls this optional scaffolding and notes that it is not developed as a full standalone pattern.
intro: Insulate clients from changing implementations while a monolith and its replacement services coexist.

unavailable.consequences: The embedded supporting passage does not give a separate wrapper trade-off discussion; the following discussion concerns strangling overall.

name: New Features as Microservices
difference: Draft title names the strategy; book names the migration action.
intro: Keep new functionality from expanding the monolith while an incremental migration is under way.

name: Transform Monolith into Microservices
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Keep the original system operating while progressively substituting domain-aligned services for its functionality.

name: Hairline Cracks
difference: Singular draft title, plural book title.
intro: Find existing seams in a monolith that can become boundaries for extracted services.

name: Extract Component
difference: The draft requires a facade; the book treats it as an option and includes recursive extraction.
intro: Move loosely connected functionality out of a monolith into an independently deployable component.

name: Macro Service
difference: The draft presents the strategy; the book names its intermediate service. The draft alias Divide and Conquer is also a book alias for Transform Monolith into Microservices; that shared phrase does not merge their identities.
intro: Extract a larger internally coupled component before refining it into smaller services.

name: Refactor then Extract
aliases: Reorganize Monolith then Extract to Microservices
difference: No matching standalone draft identified in the inspected website repository; book fallback.
intro: Reduce internal coupling before moving a portion of the monolith into a service.

name: Replace as Microservice
difference: Same core identity.
intro: Reimplement tightly coupled functionality as a service when extracting the existing code is impractical.

name: Monolith to Microservice Proxy
difference: Book shortens the draft name.
intro: Keep an existing internal interface while redirecting its implementation to a new service.

name: Playback Testing
difference: Same core identity.
intro: Compare old and new behavior by replaying captured inputs when the original system is not fully understood.
